channels.lede: Get questions and finished tasks on your phone, and answer from there. wisp reaches out to these services, so nothing needs to reach this machine. ntfy and Telegram receive titles, summaries and questions (with their context), never code or diffs.
channels.how.ntfy: Tap a button on the notification to answer
channels.how.telegram: Buttons, or reply to a message in your own words
channels.how.slack: Mention wisp, or send the bot a DM
channels.how.discord: Mention the bot, DM it, or use /wisp
channels.how.github: Comment /wisp on an issue or PR
channels.how.email: Mail a task, and the answer comes back
channels.test.title: Send a test to {name}
channels.test.sent: Test sent: it shows up like this when a task finishes or asks.
channels.test.unprompted: This channel answers only where it’s asked, so there’s nowhere to send a test. Try it from there.
channels.remove.title: Remove the saved {field}
channels.email.cloud: Email works on a cloud computer: set it up there.
channels.step.title: Set it up
channels.link.hint: Send this to the bot from the chat to link
channels.step.ntfy.on: Switch ntfy on: wisp picks a long, random topic
channels.step.ntfy.app: Install the ntfy app and subscribe to the topic
channels.step.ntfy.app.detail: Anyone who knows the topic name can read it, so keep it long and random; answers are signed, so nobody else can send them.
channels.step.telegram.bot: Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token
channels.step.telegram.link: Send the link code to your bot
channels.step.telegram.link.detail: Only the chat that sends this code gets linked.
channels.step.slack.app.detail: At api.slack.com/apps pick Create New App → From a manifest, choose your workspace and install the app.
channels.step.slack.paste.cloud: Paste the signing secret and bot token
channels.step.slack.where: App token: Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate, with the connections:write scope. Bot token: OAuth & Permissions.
channels.step.slack.where.cloud: Signing secret: Basic Information → App Credentials. Bot token: OAuth & Permissions.
channels.step.discord.app.detail: In the Developer Portal pick New Application and name it. wisp needs no privileged intent, so leave Message Content and the others off.
channels.step.discord.paste.cloud: Paste the bot token and public key
channels.step.discord.where: In the application, open Bot and press Reset Token. wisp connects as soon as it’s in.
channels.step.discord.where.cloud: Bot token: open Bot and press Reset Token. Public key: General Information.
channels.step.link.detail: In a DM to the bot, send the link code. Each code links one person, and the next shows here.
channels.step.github.gh: Sign in to the GitHub CLI on this computer
channels.step.github.gh.detail: wisp reads comments through your gh sign-in, in the repos of your projects. Only your own comments count, and Full auto can’t be asked for from there.
channels.step.github.comment: Comment /wisp on an issue or PR
channels.step.github.comment.detail: Say what you’d type in wisp: /wisp in api with opus plan: fix the flaky test
channels.step.email.sender: Add the address you’ll send from
channels.step.email.sender.detail: Your mail provider has to DKIM-sign with the same domain as your address. Consumer Gmail and iCloud do.
channels.step.email.mail.detail: Say what you’d type in wisp, in the subject or the first line. Anyone else gets no answer.
